identificationModule.briefTitle: Vitamin E Combined With Fruquintinib and Tislelizumab in Microsatellite Stabilized Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients
identificationModule.officialTitle: Phase II Clinical Study of Vitamin E Combined With Fruquintinib and Tislelizumab in Patients With Microsatellite Stabilized Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Who Failed Standard Therapy

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn about efficacy of Vitamin E in combination with Fuquinitinib and Tirelizumab in patients with microsatellite stabilized mCRC who have failed standard therapy. The main question is to explore the survival time, safety and tolerability of the treatment. At the same time, the correlation between biomarkers (including PD-L1 expression, tumor mutation load, lymphocyte subpopulation, cytokines, TCR, intestinal microbes, and others) and the efficacy and drug resistance mechanism will be analyzed, so as to provide reference for the subsequent guidance of the screening of benefit groups.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: Dietary supplements are commonly used during conventional cancer treatment. Vitamin E has a variety of functions, including enhancing immunity, anti-inflammation, and anti-oxidation. Tislelizumab is an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody, and furoquininib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that inhibits tumor angiogenesis. Studies have shown that immunotherapy combined with furoquininib has initial efficacy in the treatment of colorectal cancer. Whether vitamin E combined with immunotherapy and furoquininib can improve the prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer deserves to be studied. Therefore, the objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Vitamin E in combination with Fuquinitinib and Tirelizumab in patients with microsatellite stabilized mCRC who have failed standard therapy.

armGroups.label: Vitamin E in combination with Fuquinitinib and Tislelizumab
armGroups.description: Patients will be treated with Vitamin E, Fuquinitinib and Tislelizumab.

interventions.name: Vitamin E
interventions.description: Vitamin E: 400mg (QD), oral, once daily, continued until disease progression or intolerable toxicity.
armGroupLabels: Vitamin E in combination with Fuquinitinib and Tislelizumab

interventions.name: Fruquintinib
interventions.description: Fuquinitinib: 5mg (QD) orally for 2 weeks, 1 week off, repeated every 3 weeks until disease progression or intolerable toxicity.
armGroupLabels: Vitamin E in combination with Fuquinitinib and Tislelizumab

interventions.name: Tislelizumab
interventions.description: Tislelizumab: 200mg intravenously every 3 weeks (Q3W), was administered until the occurrence of unacceptable toxic effects, or disease progression, withdrawal of consent, or withdrawal as judged by the investigator.
armGroupLabels: Vitamin E in combination with Fuquinitinib and Tislelizumab

primaryOutcomes.description: The proportion of participants whose best outcome is complete remission or partial remission

secondaryOutcomes.description: Time from initiation of treatment to disease progression or death from any cause.
The time between the start of the participants' treatment and their death from any cause
The proportion of patients without disease progression (PD).
Assessment of the safety profile of regimen according to the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0 (NCI CTCAE v 5.0).
